Storm knocks out power to thousands

March 2, 2024

The city council voted on Tuesday to approve a sweeping new storm recovery plan that will add three light rail lines over the next decade, officials said after a marathon session that stretched past midnight.

Supporters argued the plan would cut commute times for hundreds of thousands of residents and reduce congestion on the main highways that ring the downtown core, while critics questioned the projected costs.

“This is the most significant investment in public transportation our region has seen in fifty years,” said the council president, who has championed the proposal since her election campaign two years ago.

The first line, connecting the airport to the central business district, is expected to open in 2029. Construction contracts will be tendered early next year, according to the transit authority.

Opponents, including several neighborhood associations, said they would continue to press for changes to the route, which they say would disrupt small businesses during years of construction work.

The plan still requires approval from the state legislature, which is expected to take up the measure in its spring session. Funding will come from a combination of federal grants, a new sales tax and municipal bonds.
